title: Who built it, who sold it, who closed it
lede: Roles and dates are from the sources cited. Later careers are given only where a source covers them.

people.name: Howard Deering Johnson
people.text: A grammar-school education and a failed family cigar business behind him, he bought the Wollaston store in 1925. He pioneered restaurant franchising because banks would not lend to him. Chairman and treasurer until 1964.[^1]

people.name: Howard Brennan Johnson
people.role: President from 1959; chairman and CEO until the end of 1981
people.text: Took over at 26, after Andover, Yale and Harvard Business School. Shifted the chain toward company-owned units, then froze expansion in 1974. Received $35.2M for his shares in the Imperial sale.[^1]

people.name: Pierre Franey
people.role: Vice president for menu development, from about 1960
people.text: Executive chef of Le Pavillon in New York before the founder hired him.[^19][^20]
people.later: Later a food columnist for The New York Times.[^20]

people.name: Jacques Pépin
people.text: Says he chose Howard Johnson’s over a job at the Kennedy White House. He began on the line at a Howard Johnson’s in Queens before moving to the commissary, where he and Franey worked for nearly a decade.[^19][^21][^13]
people.later: Became a television cook and author.[^19]

people.name: G. Michael Hostage
people.role: President and CEO under Imperial, from 1982
people.text: A fifteen-year Marriott veteran. Tried to integrate adjacent restaurants and lodges and let managers buy food from outside suppliers.[^1][^2]

people.name: George Carter
people.text: A second-generation franchisee who led the operators’ company formed after the 1985 breakup. In 1987 he said the chain needed to be modernized inside and out.[^4]

people.name: Carl and Joe DeSantis
people.text: Carl DeSantis opened the Lake George restaurant in 1953 and handed the family company to his son Joe in 1995. Joe closed it in 2011 and later leased it to a former employee, who reopened it in January 2015.[^13]

people.name: Ron Butler
people.text: Came to manage the Lake Placid restaurant when it opened in April 1956, bought it a few years later and ran it with his sons until March 2015.[^9]
